---
title: "Explore by area"
subtitle: "Choose a region, a combined or mayoral authority, or a local authority, and see its schools' Value Added v2.1 on a map and in a table."
toc: false
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "explore_js.R"))
source(here::here("R", "explore_data.R"))   # the schools, measures, caps and levels (shared with the trust pages)
```

Every state-funded mainstream secondary school in England has a Value
Added v2.1 figure for all pupils, disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged
pupils, girls and boys, `r yl(min(V$spec$years))` to `r yl(max(V$spec$years))`:
Attainment 8 points against England, shrunk by reliability. Choose a
level and an area; the map zooms to its schools, a chart shows how each
school's value added has moved year by year, and the table lists them.
Click a column heading to sort. "Absence against intake" is percentage
points above (positive) or below what the school's intake predicts.

**Colour by** offers the same measures as the Sussex pages, for every
school in England: value added in each of its forms, attendance (absence,
persistent absence, illness, unauthorised absence, reduced timetables,
suspensions), results, intake, and the school itself (who runs it, Ofsted,
religious character). Value added and absence against intake are coloured
on fixed national scales; the other measures run across the range within
the chosen area; a measure that is neither better nor worse high or low
(disadvantage, EAL, SEN) is shaded in greys. Whichever measure is chosen
gets a column in the table.

**Period** switches between the four-year figure (shrunk, with 95%
intervals) and a **moving average** of the yearly figures, centred on the
year you choose, over one, three or five years. A window that runs off
the end of the series uses the years there are: a three-year average
centred on `r yl(min(YEARS))` averages `r yl(YEARS[1])` and `r yl(YEARS[2])`.
Yearly figures are not shrunk, so a single year moves more than the
four-year figure; see [value added over time](method.qmd#sec-over-time).

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## `r yl(prov_year)` is provisional

The last year in the trajectories, and any moving average whose window
includes it: `r PROV_NOTE`
:::

```{r explorer}
payload <- list(
  schools = jsonlite::toJSON(dat, dataframe = "rows", na = "null", digits = 6),
  levels = jsonlite::toJSON(levels, dataframe = "rows"),
  measures = jsonlite::toJSON(measures |> mutate(cap = unname(colour_caps()[var])), dataframe = "rows", na = "null"),
  cats = cats_json(CATS)$cats, cats_s = cats_json(CATS)$cats_s,
  heads = jsonlite::toJSON(lapply(MAP_CAT_HEADS, as.list), auto_unbox = TRUE),
  none = jsonlite::toJSON(NONE, auto_unbox = TRUE),
  notes = jsonlite::toJSON(notes, auto_unbox = TRUE),
  default = jsonlite::toJSON(list(level = "ca", area = "Sussex and Brighton (new)"), auto_unbox = TRUE),
  years = jsonlite::toJSON(YEARS),
  provisional_year = jsonlite::toJSON(prov_year, auto_unbox = TRUE),
  caps_ma = jsonlite::toJSON(caps_ma, auto_unbox = TRUE))
leaflet::leaflet(height = 560, options = leaflet::leafletOptions(scrollWheelZoom = FALSE)) |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") |>
  leaflet::setView(-1.5, 52.8, 6) |>
  htmlwidgets::onRender(EXPLORE_JS, data = payload)
```

Combined and mayoral authorities are from the ONS lookup of local
authority districts to combined authorities (May 2025), with the six
Devolution Priority Programme areas announced in February 2025 added and
marked "(new)". Areas not in a combined authority are not listed at that
level. The full data are in [va_v2_schools.csv](data/va_v2_schools.csv),
and the Sussex areas have [pages of their own](sussex.qmd).
